subject: BridgePoint: recap — isolated deployment options and asks
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@bridgepointhealth.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: BridgePoint: recap — isolated deployment options and asks

Hi Laura / Marco,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clarity on regulatory scope and networking constraints. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned internally and with your infra team.

Key pain / drivers you confirmed:
- Data residency requirement: PHI must remain in-state and logs retained per state rules (7 years).
- No internet egress from model runtime: any external calls must be blocked; updates pushed via approved channels only.
- HSM/KMS policy: customer-managed keys are required; keys cannot leave customer KMS.
- Patch window and maintenance: BridgePoint will require a weekly maintenance blackout window and explicit approval for kernel/driver updates.

What we discussed as viable deployment shapes:
1) Private VPC (preferred) — Redwood control plane in our hosted region + private egress-limited compute in your VPC via secure peering and strict routing.
2) On-prem air-gapped appliance — fully isolated; offline model packaging and manual update cadence (higher upfront ops effort).
3) Hybrid (dedicated racks in a partner DC in-state) — compromise for teams that need physical locality but prefer managed ops.

Primary technical blockers we heard from infra:
- No default outbound NAT from compute subnets; all egress must be via a customer-controlled proxy.
- Limited ability to accept cross-account IAM roles without an auditor review.
- Requirement for network-level IDS/IPS inline with our serving fabric.

Immediate asks / action items (owner in parentheses):
- BridgePoint: Share the VPC network ACLs & proposed CIDR range and the security policy doc (Marco) — by EOD Tue 12/1.
- Redwood: Draft minimal firewall & peer config that satisfies the no-egress constraint and list required ports (Tessa) — by Wed 12/2.
- Redwood SRE: Provide a condensed list of kernel/driver changes that would require restart (Monica) — by Thu 12/3.
- Both: Quick thumbs-up on which deployment shape to prioritize (VPC vs on-prem) so we can prepare accurate pricing (Laura).

Attachments: bridgepoint_vpc_requirements.xlsx (network checklist), vpc_design_diagram.pdf (initial sketch).

If that matches your notes, I’ll convert this into a brief mutual action plan and share a proposed timeline.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@bridgepointhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@bridgepointhealth.com>, BridgePoint Tech <infra@bridgepointhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 00:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BridgePoint: recap — isolated deployment options and asks

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming:
- Residency: yes, in-state only.
- Egress: must be blocked from the model runtime; allowed for control-plane metadata through an audited proxy.
- KMS: we operate our own HSM; any solution must support customer-managed keys via external KMS integration.

We’ll attach the ACLs and the compliance playbook you requested (Marco will send shortly). For next step, we’re leaning towards the Private VPC approach but need your concrete egress/firewall plan to validate.

-Laura
Director of Compliance, BridgePoint Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@bridgepointhealth.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Network specifics / quick engineering clarifications

Hi Marco & Laura — Monica from Redwood SRE. A few technical clarifications to make our firewall/peering sketch precise:

1) CIDR / subnets: we need the exact compute subnet ranges and the allowed proxy IPs for control-plane callbacks.
2) Outbound: confirms that NAT is forbidden from compute subnets; our plan will route control-plane traffic via a mutually-managed proxy pair — we’ll provide the TLS SNI expectations.
3) Ports: we’ll only require 443 outbound to the proxy and inbound 10250 (health checks) from a specific Redwood-managed monitoring IP range — is that acceptable?
4) KMS integration: please confirm whether your HSM supports PKCS#11 and if we should expect key encryption/decryption to happen entirely within your HSM.

I’ve attached a lightweight diagram (vpc_design_diagram.pdf) and a short checklist (bridgepoint_vpc_requirements.xlsx). If you can return the CIDR + HSM details we’ll produce the peer/firewall template.

Regards,
Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): vpc_design_diagram.pdf (diagram), bridgepoint_vpc_requirements.xlsx (checklist)
